translations.text: The Book of Susanna.
There was a man living in Babylon whose name was Joakim.
He married a woman named Susanna, the daughter of Helna. She was very beautiful and feared the Lord.
All her family were righteous, and they taught their daughter all the commandments of Moses.
Her husband Joakim was extremely wealthy. He had a garden around his house, and the Jews would gather at his house, because he was more distinguished than all of them at that time.

Two elders arose among the people, who were the people's [?] and judges that year. It was about them that God said, “Wickedness came out of Babylon, from them—from the elders and judges who served in the temple.”
These men used to come regularly to Joakim's house, and everyone who had a legal dispute would come and have their case heard.
When all the people had gone away at midday, Susanna would go with her maids into her husband's garden.
Those elders saw her every day as she walked about and went into her husband's garden.
They lusted after her, and their minds became corrupted. They lowered their eyes so that they would not look toward heaven or be remembered any longer among the righteous.
Both of them lusted after her, wanting to be with her as a man is with a woman, but they did not reveal their affliction to one another,
because they wanted to be with her secretly.
Every day they eagerly watched for her, hoping to see her.
One said to his companion, “Let us leave here, because it is time for the meal.”

They went out to leave together, but each slipped away from the other. Both turned back without the other's knowledge, and when they came, they met one another there. Ashamed of the way they had deceived each other, they sat down and revealed to one another their lustful and destructive desire: how they lusted after this woman who was full of chastity. From then on they watched for an opportunity to find her alone and dishonor this woman who deserved to be remembered with honor.

While they were watching for her, they saw her coming as she did every day, just as she had the day before and the day before that, with her two maids. She wanted to bathe there in the gardens because it was hot. Those elders went and hid there in the garden.
There was no one else in the garden except those two elders.
Susanna said to her maids, “Go and bring me oil and soap, and shut the garden gates while I bathe.”
They did as she had commanded them. They shut the garden gate and went to bring what they had been told to bring. They did not see those elders who were hiding there.
When Susanna's maids had gone out, those elders rushed at her and said to her,
“Look, the garden gates are shut, and there is no one to see us. Since we desire you, sleep with us.
But if you are unwilling to sleep with us, we will testify falsely against you that a young man slept with you, and that this was why you sent your maids away from you.”

Susanna considered this and said, “I am hemmed in on every side. If I do this, it means death for me before God, because I will have dishonored the bed of Joakim my husband. And if I do not do it, I will suffer a cruel death at your hands, along with a bad reputation unworthy of my freeborn status. I will leave my whole family in shame because of the false testimony of wicked men, who add to Israel's ruin and misery by making it a mockery among foreign nations.
But it is better for me to die at your hands, you wicked men, than to sin before the Lord, from whom nothing is hidden. I trust in him to rescue me even from your hands.”
Susanna cried out loudly because of the distress she suffered at the hands of these lustful men, and those elders also shouted against her.
One of them ran and opened the gates of the garden.

When this cry was heard in the garden, the members of Susanna’s household ran in quickly to see what had happened to her. When all Susanna’s people had gathered, those elders began to give false testimony against her: “As we were passing outside the garden, we peered in to look at the garden and saw Susanna with a young man lying with her. We ran to seize them, but we could not seize the young man because he was stronger than we were.”
When all Susanna’s people heard the elders’ words, they were ashamed of what the elders said she had done.

The next day all the people gathered at the home of Joakim, her husband, to investigate Susanna’s case. If she had really committed this defilement and dishonored the bed of Joakim, her husband, she was to die. Those two elders also came to accuse her unjustly.
They said before all the people, “Send for Susanna, the daughter of Helkanah, Joakim’s wife.” And they sent for her.
She came with her entire family and all her acquaintances and friends, and she stood in the middle of the whole assembly of the people.
She was a very beautiful woman, humbler than all the other women, and very modest in her dress.
When those wicked men saw her, they ordered her veil to be removed, so that they might at least satisfy themselves by looking at her beauty.
Everyone who saw her was weeping, together with all her people.
While a large crowd surrounded her, those two elders came forward and gave false testimony against her. They placed their hands on Susanna’s head and said, “We saw this woman lying with a young man.”
Susanna, deeply distressed by what had happened to her, lifted her eyes toward heaven, toward the Lord, because her heart was set on God.

Those two elders said, “Yesterday, while we were walking outside the garden, Susanna came with her two servant girls, and they entered the garden. She sent her maids away and shut the gates of the garden.
Then a young man who had been hiding came to her and lay with her.
We had entered the garden, and we saw the deceit and ran toward them.
We found them lying together, but we could not seize the young man because he was stronger than we were. He opened the gate of the garden and escaped.
But we seized this woman and asked her, ‘Who is that young man who was lying with you?’ She would not tell us who he was. We testify to these things against her before you.”

The whole assembly believed them because they were elders of the people and judges. They condemned Susanna to death, so that all women would be afraid and would never again bring such disgrace upon themselves and their families.
Susanna cried out in a loud voice and said, “God, who knows all things, before whom hidden things lie revealed, who knows what is to come before it happens—

may he see that these men have accused me falsely. Here I am about to die, although I have done none of the things they have testified against me, but only because I did not fulfill their desire by doing what they asked of me.”
The Lord heard Susanna’s cry.
As she was going out to die, God immediately sent his Holy Spirit upon a young boy named Daniel.
He cried out in a loud voice and said, “I am innocent of this woman’s blood, because she is innocent of this defilement.”
The whole assembly turned toward him and said to him, “What is this that you have said?”
Standing among them, he answered, “Are you so foolish, people of Israel, that you do not judge the daughters of Israel justly?”
Return to the court, for you have falsely condemned this woman.
The whole assembly returned to the court, and those elders said to Daniel, “Come, sit among us and speak to us. Let us see, for God has given you the standing of an elder.”

Daniel said to the whole assembly, “Separate these elders from one another for me. Then I will judge them as God enables me, and I will show that they have unjustly given false testimony against Susanna.”
The assembly separated them from one another. He called one of them and said to him, “You have grown old in evil days. Now the sins you committed long ago have caught up with you,
for you gave unjust judgments, condemned the righteous, destroyed the humble, acquitted the guilty, and condemned the innocent.
Now tell me this before this whole assembly: under which tree did you see this woman and that young man lying together?” The elder said to him, “Under a pistachio tree.”
Daniel said to him, “But know this: if you have indeed lied, it will come down on your own head. For God’s angel is [?]; he has received a command from God to split you from end to end.”
Afterward he called the other man, his companion, and said to him as well, “You offspring of Canaan, not of Judah! This woman’s beauty enslaved you, and desire for her turned your heart.
This is how you used to treat the daughters of Israel, and out of fear they would carry out your evil wishes.

But you, tell me before this whole assembly: under which tree did you see this woman and that young man lying together?” He answered before the whole assembly, “Under a pomegranate tree.” The whole assembly shouted together with a loud voice and praised the Lord, who reveals hidden things, rewards the innocent according to their innocence, repays the unjust, and brings their conduct down on their own heads.

Daniel said to him, “You have truly spoken unjustly before the Lord against this defenseless woman. You wanted to shed innocent blood unjustly. But now your wickedness will come down on your own head, as it is written in the law of Moses. For look, God’s angel has been sent against you, holding a sword in his hand, to split you from end to end and destroy both of you together.”
The whole assembly answered together with a loud voice, “Glory to God, who has given life to all who have believed in his name!”
Daniel exposed the wrong they had done, and the whole assembly rose against them.
They dealt with them according to Moses’ command and put them to death. The Lord brought evil retribution upon them, as they deserved, and innocent blood was spared that day.

Elkanah and his wife rejoiced over their daughter Susanna, Joakim’s wife, because no wrongdoing had been found in her. All the people and Susanna’s entire family praised God because the disgrace of wrongdoing had been removed from them.

Daniel grew in prominence and found favor with Susanna’s entire family and in the eyes of the whole assembly of Israel. He always practiced justice and righteousness. The fame of his praiseworthy deeds was spoken of among all the people, along with the hidden and secret things he had discerned. The book of Susanna is finished.
